Hi Lara — thanks for the clear asks, great questions. Short answer up front: we commit that customer content is not used to train or improve our production models. Below I’ve laid out operational nuance and the practical purge flow so your procurement/legal teams have precise language to work with. I’m copying our privacy and infra leads for verification.

1) Modeling assurance (what we mean by “we do not train on your data”):
- Redwood does not feed customer request/response data into model training pipelines, fine-tuning jobs, or public model update processes. Model training systems are isolated and require explicit, auditable dataset ingestion steps.
- Exception: with explicit, documented consent we may use anonymized, opt-in datasets for internal research; this is opt-in only and governed by a separate research agreement.

2) Operational artifacts and short-term retention:
- Request/response logs and traces: retained for operational monitoring and debugging for up to 30 days by default. These logs are accessible only to on-call/ops personnel and are not eligible for training pipelines.
- Debug snapshots / KV caches: transient debug snapshots (used for reproducing incidents) are retained for up to 7 days and then deleted automatically unless flagged for longer retention during an open incident investigation.
- Telemetry and aggregated metrics: retained in aggregated, pseudonymized form for product analytics; no raw customer text is used for model updates.

3) Purge semantics (how deletion requests are handled):
- Tombstone (immediate): within 24 hours of a valid deletion API call or support ticket the account’s live access to data is revoked and identifiers are tombstoned so the data is no longer queryable in production.
- Hot/nearline erase: within 30 days we remove customer content from primary serving stores and ephemeral caches. This is the operational deletion that makes data inaccessible to live systems.
- Backups & snapshots: we retain encrypted backups/snapshots per our backup policy (default rotation window up to 90 days) to meet availability and disaster recovery commitments. Backups are immutable for the retention window; they are scheduled for deletion at the end of the retention window and are not used for any training or research.
- Legal holds & export requests: deletion is paused if a valid legal hold is present; for export requests we provide a one-time export and start the deletion timeline upon confirmation.

4) Evidence & attestation:
- We can provide a signed attestation (attached) that references your account id (RD-ACME-2026) and repeats the no-training commitment plus the operational windows above.
- For high-assurance customers we can arrange a one-time deletion verification: after the purge we will provide an operational log extract showing the tombstone event and subsequent archive deletion timestamps.

5) Control knobs for enterprise customers:
- Dedicated and Private deployments: you can configure retention TTLs, disable short-term logging, and route telemetry out to your own sinks. For Private deployments, the default is no retention beyond request processing unless you enable diagnostic dumps.
- API deletion: DELETE /v1/accounts/{id}/data triggers the tombstone workflow; support ticket acts as backup if you need human verification.

Next steps: I’ve attached our quick retention matrix (data_retention_matrix.xlsx) and a draft no-training attestation (no-training-attestation.pdf). Mina, Lauren — could you confirm the debug snapshot 7-day default and attach the attestation with signature if acceptable?

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call with infra and legal to walk Acme procurement through the checklist.
